question.text: Projectiles <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> are thrown at angles of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with vertical respectively from top of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>400</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> high tower. If their times of flight are same, the ratio of their speeds of projection <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></math> is:

solution.text:
For same time of flight, vertical component of velocity of projection must be same. Therefore,

vAsin45°=vBsin30°⇒vAvB=1212⇒vAvB=12
